# Agent tools

The tools bb-box gives a thread's agent, with their parameters as the agent sees them.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`box_acquire`](#box_acquire) | Get a fresh box for this thread: a Linux or macOS computer for commands, builds, tests, servers or Docker, away from the thread's own machine. |
| [`box_copy`](#box_copy) | Copy one file, of any size, between this thread's workspace or its storage folder ($BB_THREAD_STORAGE) and a box. |
| [`box_device`](#box_device) | Control an ios or android box's device, as the panel's toolbar does: Home, Back and Recents, lock and wake, rotate, fold, appearance, text size, location, status bar, battery, network, install an app, switch device, and reboot. |
| [`box_enrol`](#box_enrol) | Add a ready box that could not join BB, or is not a BB machine, to BB again, so threads can run on it. |
| [`box_fork`](#box_fork) | Make a new box of this thread from a snapshot of one of its boxes, or from the box as it is now, to try two things from one set-up state. |
| [`box_grant`](#box_grant) | Grant a program in a macOS box macOS permissions, such as Accessibility or Screen Recording, with no prompt. |
| [`box_image_draft`](#box_image_draft) | Draft a project image's script (049) from the project's own files, for you to finish, try with box_image_try and register with box_image_set. |
| [`box_image_set`](#box_image_set) | Set this thread's project's image (049): a shell script run as root on the standard image of its kinds, so the project's boxes start with what it needs, such as a language's toolchain. |
| [`box_image_try`](#box_image_try) | Try a project image's script as a build runs it (049), before box_image_set: in a new box of the kind's current standard image, on a backend that builds images, the script runs as root with BB_BOX_IMAGE, BB_BOX_KIND, BB_BOX_BACKEND and BB_BOX_ARCH, then the check as the box user, then finalizing, which empties /tmp, /var/tmp and the caches. |
| [`box_job`](#box_job) | Get the exit code and output of a box_run command that went on in its box as a job: one still running after 270 s, or when bb-box restarted, as for an update. |
| [`box_list`](#box_list) | List this thread's boxes and the kinds of box you can acquire. |
| [`box_record`](#box_record) | Record a desktop box's screen, to show your work in the thread as a short video (059). |
| [`box_release`](#box_release) | Release a box you no longer need. |
| [`box_resize`](#box_resize) | Change a box's size: its cores, memory or disk, by a preset or by parts, where its backend can. |
| [`box_restore`](#box_restore) | Restore a box to one of its snapshots when an attempt went wrong, rather than undoing it by hand. |
| [`box_run`](#box_run) | Run a shell script in a box, as its user, and wait for it. |
| [`box_snapshot`](#box_snapshot) | Take a snapshot of a box: its disk, or with memory its disk and running apps where its backend can, so you can restore it if a change goes wrong. |
| [`box_snapshot_delete`](#box_snapshot_delete) | Delete a snapshot of a box that an agent of this thread took and nobody kept. |
| [`box_snapshots`](#box_snapshots) | List the snapshots of a box, or of every box of this thread and the machine it runs on: per box, what its snapshots hold or that it has none; per snapshot, its name, ID, when, by whom, what it holds, its size, its price, whether it is kept, and where it is. |
| [`box_start`](#box_start) | Start a stopped box again, with its disk as it was, and wait up to 20 s more while it reconnects as a BB machine. |
| [`box_status`](#box_status) | Show one box: its state, kind, address, whether it is a BB machine, and how long it took to start and to become one. |
| [`box_stop`](#box_stop) | Stop a box to free its memory and CPU while keeping its disk. |
| [`box_thread`](#box_thread) | Start a child thread on a box, as a BB machine, in this thread's project, with the task as its prompt. |
| [`computer_act`](#computer_act) | Click, double-click, right-click, scroll or set a value on a desktop or device box: on an element by its reference from computer_observe, or at x and y in your latest image of a window or the desktop. |
| [`computer_launch`](#computer_launch) | Open an app on a desktop box by its name or path, or open a URL in the box's browser. |
| [`computer_observe`](#computer_observe) | Read a window on a desktop or device box as text: its accessibility tree, one element per line, with a reference such as e12 for each element you can act on, and on a device the element's identifier where the app gives one. |
| [`computer_screenshot`](#computer_screenshot) | Take an image of a window on a desktop box, or of the whole desktop, or of a device box's screen. |
| [`computer_take_control`](#computer_take_control) | Take control of a desktop box's desktop, or a device box's device, back from a person who took it in BB, so the computer tools work again. |
| [`computer_type`](#computer_type) | Type text, or press a key or chord such as Escape, Return, Tab, ctrl+a or ctrl+shift+t, into an element by its reference, or into the focused element of a window. |
| [`computer_windows`](#computer_windows) | List the windows on a desktop box's screen, with the window IDs the other computer tools take. |

## box_acquire

Get a fresh box for this thread: a Linux or macOS computer for commands, builds, tests, servers or Docker, away from the thread's own machine. It starts in seconds and stays until you release it or the thread ends.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | string | no | The kind, from box_list: linux, linux-desktop and the rest, or linux-docker for a linux box that must have Docker. Defaults to the user's default kind. |
| `size` | string | no | small, medium or large. Defaults to the kind's default preset; box_list shows each kind's sizes. |
| `cores` | integer | no | Cores, for a custom size. Parts you leave out come from the preset. |
| `memory_gib` | integer | no | Memory in GiB, for a custom size: at least 2 for a Linux box. |
| `disk_gib` | integer | no | Root disk in GiB, for a custom size. Presets keep the kind's own disk. |
| `wait` | boolean | no | Wait until the box answers, and up to 20 s more while it becomes a BB machine. Defaults to true. |
| `on` | string or array of string | no | Where the box goes, from box_list: a provider such as Docker on devpc, or a list of them for the first with room among them. Leave it out for the first with room. |
| `image` | string | no | The image the box starts from, from box_list: a project's image by name, or "standard" for bb-box's own. Leave it out for this project's image for the kind, or the standard one. |
| `device` | string | no | For an ios or android box, the device it boots, from box_list, such as iPhone 18 Pro or Pixel Fold. Defaults to the kind's first. |
| `slim` | boolean | no | For an ios box: its iOS Simulator runs without the services a device box does not need, such as widgets, Siri, iCloud, Health and Wallet, for about a quarter of the memory and almost no idle CPU. Defaults to true. Set false for an app that uses one of them. |
| `gpu` | `none`, `shared`, `whole` | no | The box's GPU: none; shared, one card other boxes may share; or whole, a card to itself, on which bb-box places no other box, where this install has whole cards on. Left out: shared for linux-desktop, none for linux. Only linux and linux-desktop take one, where a provider has cards; box_list says which do, the room on each card, and whether whole cards are on. |
| `dedicated` | boolean | no | For an ios box: a macOS VM of its own, with sudo, brew install, its own cores, ports and desktop, instead of a macOS user on a shared host. It takes one of the Mac's two VMs, so it may wait for one. Without it, an ios box is shared where a shared iOS host has room, and a VM of its own otherwise. Give it with a size, cores, memory_gib or disk_gib: where a shared iOS host is set up, a size without it is refused. |
| `shared` | boolean | no | For an ios box: a macOS user on a Mac or VM shared with other ios boxes, ready in seconds, with its own device, files and keychain, but no sudo, Homebrew installs or app windows; an ios box is one already where a shared iOS host has room, and shared: true refuses rather than give it a VM of its own. For a macos box: a macOS user on a Mac or VM shared with ios boxes, ready in seconds, for commands, builds and the iOS Simulator, with its own files and keychain, but no sudo, Homebrew installs, desktop or app windows, and cores, ports and processes shared. Only where a shared iOS host is set up; box_list says. Without it a macos box is a VM of its own, which takes one of the Mac's two VMs. |

## box_copy

Copy one file, of any size, between this thread's workspace or its storage folder ($BB_THREAD_STORAGE) and a box. Every copy's size and SHA-256 are checked at both ends, and one that does not match fails. A file over 16 MiB streams through bb-box's worker on the thread's machine. A relative path on this side is under the workspace; a path under the storage folder, absolute or starting with $BB_THREAD_STORAGE/, is there. A relative box path, or one starting with ~/, is under the box user's home. Tar a directory first.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `direction` | `to_box`, `from_box` | yes | to_box copies from the workspace or storage folder into the box; from_box copies from the box into the workspace or storage folder. |
| `from` | string | yes | The file to copy. |
| `to` | string | no | Where to put it. Defaults to the file's own name, in the box user's home or in the workspace's directory. |

## box_device

Control an ios or android box's device, as the panel's toolbar does: Home, Back and Recents, lock and wake, rotate, fold, appearance, text size, location, status bar, battery, network, install an app, switch device, and reboot. Each action takes only its own parameters. The answer says what happened, how long it took, and the device's state after it. While a person has control of the box, every action but install is refused, and so is an install that would replace an installed app. Screenshots, taps and URLs are the computer tools'.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `action` | `home`, `back`, `recents`, `lock`, `wake`, `rotate`, `posture`, `appearance`, `text_size`, `location`, `status_bar`, `battery`, `network`, `install`, `switch`, `reboot` | yes | What to do. iOS has no back, recents, posture or network; only foldables take posture. box_status lists the device's actions. |
| `turn` | `left`, `right` | no | rotate: a quarter turn from where the device is, the way the toolbar's arrows point. |
| `to` | string or number | no | rotate: upright, turned-left, upside-down, turned-right. posture: closed, half-open, open. appearance: light, dark. text_size: larger, smaller, default, or a step of the platform: an iOS content size from extra-small to accessibility-extra-extra-extra-large, such as accessibility-large, or an Android font scale such as 1.3. status_bar: clean, live. network: online, offline, slow. |
| `latitude` | number | no | location: with longitude, from -90 to 90. Leave both out to clear the simulated location. |
| `longitude` | number | no | location: with latitude, from -180 to 180. |
| `level` | number | no | battery: with charging, a whole number from 0 to 100. Leave both out for the device's own. On iOS only the status bar's picture changes. |
| `charging` | boolean | no | battery: with level, whether it charges. |
| `paths` | array of string | no | install: in the box, as box_copy puts them there. On iOS one .app folder built for the simulator; on Android one .apk, or the split APKs of one app. |
| `device` | string | no | switch: a model this box offers, from box_list, such as iPhone 17. Each model keeps its own apps and data. |

## box_enrol

Add a ready box that could not join BB, or is not a BB machine, to BB again, so threads can run on it. BB's installer runs in it as its user. It does not restart, stop or resize the box. It stops only the BB daemon of a machine that BB no longer has. A box whose machine BB still has is left as it is, and recorded as a BB machine.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |

## box_fork

Make a new box of this thread from a snapshot of one of its boxes, or from the box as it is now, to try two things from one set-up state. The fork gets the snapshot's files and its own identity: a new BB machine, address and keys, so it never acts as its source. Everything else on the disk comes with it, project secrets and signed-in browsers too. It starts fresh, with no apps running, at the snapshot's size.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box to fork, by its name or ID: one of this thread's boxes, not one it runs on. |
| `snapshot` | string | no | The snapshot's name or ID, from box_snapshots. Left out, bb-box takes one of the box now, named "for a fork", and forks that. |
| `name` | string | no | The new box's name: a lower-case letter first, then letters, digits and "-", up to 32, not ending in "-". One is made up when left out. |
| `gpu` | `none`, `shared`, `whole` | no | The fork's GPU. none, the default, starts it with no card. shared places a shared card, and whole a card to itself where this install has whole cards on, before anything is copied; only a desktop can take either. |

## box_grant

Grant a program in a macOS box macOS permissions, such as Accessibility or Screen Recording, with no prompt. On Tart's macOS boxes, and on Macs of the SSH host pool with SIP off; Linux and Windows boxes refuse. The program must be the box user's, or an app in /Applications, and signed: sign it with the box's identity, codesign -s "bb-box local code signing", so a rebuild keeps the grant. Commands box_run runs have the microphone and camera already.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `program` | string | yes | The app's path, such as /Users/bbx-3/Applications/Probe.app, or a program's full path in the box. |
| `permissions` | array of `accessibility`, `screen-recording`, `input-monitoring`, `microphone`, `camera`, `system-audio`, `automation` | yes | The permissions to grant. |
| `target` | string | no | For automation: the bundle ID of the app the program sends Apple events to, such as com.apple.finder. |

## box_image_draft

Draft a project image's script (049) from the project's own files, for you to finish, try with box_image_try and register with box_image_set. Read these from the repository and pass each one's path and text: .devcontainer/devcontainer.json (or .devcontainer.json, or one in a subfolder of .devcontainer) and the Dockerfile it names; a Dockerfile; .tool-versions; mise.toml; .nvmrc or .node-version; .python-version; rust-toolchain.toml or rust-toolchain; flake.nix with flake.lock, or shell.nix. It returns a script for .bb/box-setup.sh, each part commented with the file it came from, a check for .bb/box-check.sh, and what it could not translate. The script runs as root on bb-box's standard Ubuntu 24.04 image, with no checkout of the repository: what needs one, such as npm ci, stays in the thread. With `box`, it also reads what a Linux box of this thread has that its image had not, for a box someone set up by hand: packages, package sources, npm globals, mise's tools, the Rust toolchain, uv tools, and what is new in /usr/local, /opt and ~/.local/bin.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | array of object | yes | The project's files the draft reads. An empty list gives a template. |
| `box` | string | no | A Linux box of this thread to read what was set up in it by hand, by name or ID. |

## box_image_set

Set this thread's project's image (049): a shell script run as root on the standard image of its kinds, so the project's boxes start with what it needs, such as a language's toolchain. Pass the files' text: commit them in the repository as .bb/box-setup.sh and .bb/box-check.sh, and give their paths. The script runs in a booted box with the network, on any Linux backend, and reads BB_BOX_IMAGE, BB_BOX_KIND, BB_BOX_BACKEND and BB_BOX_ARCH where it must differ. It gets none of the project's secrets. Setting it changes every new box of those kinds in the project, so ask the user first unless they asked for it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | The image's name, such as "rust-tools": a lower-case letter first, then letters, digits and "-". |
| `kinds` | array of string | yes | The Linux kinds it builds on, such as ["linux", "linux-desktop-cpu"]. box_list shows the kinds. |
| `script` | string | yes | The script's text, run as root. |
| `check` | string | no | A check's text, run as the box user after the script, such as `cargo --version`: the image fails when it fails. |
| `bake` | `auto`, `always`, `never` | no | auto (the default) builds it ahead once two boxes started within 14 days; always keeps a build; never runs the script at each start. |
| `script_path` | string | no | The script's path in the repository, such as .bb/box-setup.sh. |
| `check_path` | string | no | The check's path in the repository, such as .bb/box-check.sh. |

## box_image_try

Try a project image's script as a build runs it (049), before box_image_set: in a new box of the kind's current standard image, on a backend that builds images, the script runs as root with BB_BOX_IMAGE, BB_BOX_KIND, BB_BOX_BACKEND and BB_BOX_ARCH, then the check as the box user, then finalizing, which empties /tmp, /var/tmp and the caches. A box of the build then runs the check again and the kind's own check. It returns each check's result, the time and the build's last 200 lines, and removes the boxes and the build, unless keep is true, when a box of it stays for you to look inside. Each try starts from a clean standard image, as a build does, so fix the script and try again until every check passes. It can take as long as the script, plus about a minute.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | string | yes | The Linux kind to try it on, such as "linux". box_list shows the kinds. |
| `script` | string | yes | The script's text, run as root, as in .bb/box-setup.sh. |
| `check` | string | no | The check's text, run as the box user, as in .bb/box-check.sh: it should fail when the script did not do its work. |
| `name` | string | no | The image's name, which the script reads as BB_BOX_IMAGE. "try" when left out. |
| `on` | string | no | A backend's ID from box_list, such as proxmox-lxc. The first that builds the kind's images when left out. |
| `keep` | boolean | no | Keep a box of what it built, to look inside with box_run: of the build, or of the build box as a failing script left it. It is this thread's box until you release it. |

## box_job

Get the exit code and output of a box_run command that went on in its box as a job: one still running after 270 s, or when bb-box restarted, as for an update. box_run's answer names the job.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `job` | string | yes | The job's ID, from box_run's error. |

## box_list

List this thread's boxes and the kinds of box you can acquire.

It takes no parameters.

## box_record

Record a desktop box's screen, to show your work in the thread as a short video (059). start begins recording and returns at once: then do what the video should show, with the computer tools and box_run. While recording, step captions what you test next ("It keeps the draft when saving fails"), and result gives its outcome with passed true or false ("Draft kept; no error toast"); both are burned into the clip and listed as chapters, at the top of the video, or at the bottom with position "bottom" at start, which suits a check near the top of the screen, such as a menu bar or a window's title. A cut still stretch shows "▶▶ 18 s later" in a corner, and a faster clip its speed. stop ends it and makes the clip in this thread's storage folder, with a page that plays it in the thread. Still stretches are cut to half a second unless stills is "keep". A recording ends by itself after 5 minutes, and stop still gives its clip. Linux desktops, on X11 and Wayland, macOS and Windows desktops. On an ios or android box it records the device's own screen, not the host's: the device in its frame, turning as it turns, with touches shown as circles and the captions in a band above or below it; a stretch the device or its server lost is captioned in the clip.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `action` | `start`, `step`, `result`, `stop` | yes | start begins recording; step captions the next check; result gives its outcome; stop ends it and makes the clip. |
| `text` | string | no | With step: what you check next. With result: what you saw. One short line each. |
| `passed` | boolean | no | With result: whether the check passed. |
| `position` | `top`, `bottom` | no | With start: where step captions go. Defaults to "top"; "bottom" when what you check is near the top of the screen. |
| `speed` | number or number or number | no | With stop: the clip plays this many times faster. Defaults to 1. |
| `stills` | `cut`, `keep` | no | With stop: cut each still stretch to half a second (the default), or keep it. |

## box_release

Release a box you no longer need. Its disk and everything on it are deleted. Copy out anything you want to keep first.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |

## box_resize

Change a box's size: its cores, memory or disk, by a preset or by parts, where its backend can. Parts left out stay as they are, and the disk only grows. A change that needs a restart is made only with restart true. check true only says what would change.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `size` | string | no | small, medium or large, from box_list: the preset's cores and memory. The disk stays as it is. |
| `cores` | integer | no | Cores. Left out, the box keeps its own. |
| `memory_gib` | integer | no | Memory in GiB: at least 2 for a Linux box. Left out, the box keeps its own. |
| `disk_gib` | integer | no | Root disk in GiB, which only grows. Left out, the box keeps its own. |
| `restart` | boolean | no | Allow a restart, which ends everything running in the box, where a part needs one. Defaults to false: bb-box then changes nothing and says so. |
| `check` | boolean | no | Only say what the resize would change, how, and whether there is room. Defaults to false. |

## box_restore

Restore a box to one of its snapshots when an attempt went wrong, rather than undoing it by hand. Everything on its disk since then goes, and the box restarts, so every process in it ends. bb-box always takes an undo first, a snapshot of the box once stopped. While Settings turn agents' restores off, this opens a form for a yes given in the thread and answers at once: then end your turn. A box this thread or another runs on, or one of the person's machines, is restored only through such a form, and only where bb-box allows it; this says so when it does not.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `snapshot` | string | yes | The snapshot's name or ID, from box_snapshots. |
| `replace` | boolean | yes | Must be true: you mean to replace the box's disk with the snapshot's. |
| `request` | string | no | An ID you make, so a repeat of this call is the same restore, not a second one. |

## box_run

Run a shell script in a box, as its user, and wait for it. You get the exit code, stdout and stderr. box_status says whether the box user can use sudo.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `command` | string | yes | A shell script, run by the box user's shell (bash on Linux, PowerShell 7 on Windows). |
| `cwd` | string | no | Directory to run in. Defaults to the box user's home. |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | no | Seconds before the command, and everything it started, is stopped. Defaults to 600. box_run returns when the script's shell exits, or after 270 s, as BB ends a tool call at about five minutes: a command still running then goes on as a job for box_job, except a Windows one in the desktop session, which is stopped then. Start a server in the background with its output redirected, so it keeps working after that: nohup &lt;cmd> >server.log 2>&1 &, or on Windows Start-Detached { &lt;cmd> } server.log |
| `stdin` | string | no | Text to send to the command's standard input. |
| `desktop` | boolean | no | Run in the box's desktop session so it can open windows. Desktop boxes only. |

## box_snapshot

Take a snapshot of a box: its disk, or with memory its disk and running apps where its backend can, so you can restore it if a change goes wrong. Take one before a change you cannot undo, such as a migration, an upgrade, a deletion or a change to the system, and when the person asks; never on a schedule of your own.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `name` | string | no | Its name, at most 60 characters, unique on the box, such as "before the migration". The time, such as Thu 10:42, when left out. |
| `note` | string | no | A note, at most 1 KB: what the box held, or why you took it. |
| `memory` | boolean | no | Hold the box's memory too, so a restore brings back its running apps: only where its backend can, and slower. Defaults to false where its backend can leave it out, and to true where every snapshot holds it, as on a macOS box on Tart, where false is refused. |

## box_snapshot_delete

Delete a snapshot of a box that an agent of this thread took and nobody kept. A kept snapshot, the person's and another thread's are the person's to delete.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `snapshot` | string | yes | The snapshot's name or ID, from box_snapshots. |

## box_snapshots

List the snapshots of a box, or of every box of this thread and the machine it runs on: per box, what its snapshots hold or that it has none; per snapshot, its name, ID, when, by whom, what it holds, its size, its price, whether it is kept, and where it is.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | no | The box's name or ID. Every box of this thread, and the machine it runs on, when left out. |

## box_stop

Stop a box to free its memory and CPU while keeping its disk. box_start starts it again.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |

## box_thread

Start a child thread on a box, as a BB machine, in this thread's project, with the task as its prompt. It works in a worktree of the project's repository on the box, cloned there once, and is archived with this thread.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `prompt` | string | yes | The child thread's first message: the task it should do on the box. |
| `title` | string | no | A title for the child thread. Defaults to "On box &lt;name>". |

## computer_act

Click, double-click, right-click, scroll or set a value on a desktop or device box: on an element by its reference from computer_observe, or at x and y in your latest image of a window or the desktop. Or press a key or chord with action key and keys, as computer_type does. On a device box a click is a tap, right_click a long press of 1.2 s, scroll a swipe within the list that holds the element, which stops at the list's end, set_value sets text fields only, and drag drags from ref or x and y to to_x and to_y, as for a slider. Says what changed in the window, which menus or popups opened or closed, and on the desktop which windows opened, closed or changed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `action` | `click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `scroll`, `set_value`, `key`, `drag` | yes | What to do: click, double_click or right_click on ref or at x and y; scroll in direction; set_value to value; key to press keys; drag, on a device box, to to_x and to_y. |
| `ref` | string | no | The element's reference from computer_observe, such as e12. |
| `window` | integer or string or string | no | With x and y: the window whose image they are pixels of, or "desktop". For key without ref: the window that gets the key, or "desktop" for whatever has the focus. |
| `x` | integer | no | Pixels from the left of your latest image of the window. |
| `y` | integer | no | Pixels from the top of your latest image of the window. |
| `value` | string | no | For set_value: the value, such as a field's text or a slider's number. |
| `direction` | `up`, `down`, `left`, `right` | no | For scroll. |
| `amount` | integer | no | For scroll: how many steps. Defaults to 3. |
| `keys` | string | no | For key: the key or chord, such as Escape or ctrl+a. |
| `to_x` | integer | no | For drag: where to drag to, in pixels from the left of your latest image of the device. |
| `to_y` | integer | no | For drag: where to drag to, in pixels from the top of your latest image of the device. |

## computer_launch

Open an app on a desktop box by its name or path, or open a URL in the box's browser. Says which windows it opened; for a URL, waits up to 10 s for the page's title. On a device box, open an app by its bundle ID or package, such as com.apple.Preferences or com.android.settings, or its name, such as Settings, or open a URL, which the device's own handler takes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `app` | string | no | The app's name, such as firefox or mousepad, or the path of its program. On a device, its bundle ID or package, or its name. |
| `url` | string | no | A URL to open in the default browser. |

## computer_observe

Read a window on a desktop or device box as text: its accessibility tree, one element per line, with a reference such as e12 for each element you can act on, and on a device the element's identifier where the app gives one. Pass query to see only matching elements, or screenshot for an image of the window as well.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `window` | integer | yes | The window's ID, from computer_windows or computer_launch. |
| `query` | string | no | Show only elements whose line contains this text, ignoring case, with their ancestors. |
| `limit` | integer | no | How many lines of the tree to show. Defaults to 300. |
| `screenshot` | boolean | no | Also return an image of the window. Defaults to false. |

## computer_screenshot

Take an image of a window on a desktop box, or of the whole desktop, or of a device box's screen. Use it when appearance matters or the tree does not show what you need. Pixels you give computer_act are pixels of your latest image of that window, which may be smaller than the window or screen: the result says the scale.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `window` | integer or string or string | no | The window's ID, or "desktop" for the whole screen. Defaults to "desktop". |

## computer_take_control

Take control of a desktop box's desktop, or a device box's device, back from a person who took it in BB, so the computer tools work again. Keys they held down are let go, and the desktop gets back its size. Use it when the person asks you to continue, or when the thread makes clear they have finished; otherwise wait for them to hand control back.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |

## computer_type

Type text, or press a key or chord such as Escape, Return, Tab, ctrl+a or ctrl+shift+t, into an element by its reference, or into the focused element of a window. On a device box, text a US keyboard has goes as keys and the rest as one paste; cmd is the Command key on iOS, and ctrl+a selects all on Android, where ctrl+v pastes nothing in Chrome: send the text instead. On a device, text into an element waits after the tap that focuses it, up to 5 s, until a field has the focus and its keyboard shows. For an open menu or popup, give its window ID, or window "desktop" for whatever has the focus. Says what the element reads afterwards.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
| `text` | string | no | Characters to type. |
| `keys` | string | no | One key or chord to press, such as Escape, Return, Tab, ctrl+a or ctrl+shift+t: modifiers and a key joined by "+". Write ctrl++ for ctrl and the + key. |
| `ref` | string | no | The element's reference from computer_observe, such as e12. |
| `window` | integer or string or string | no | Without ref: the window whose focused element gets the input, a menu or popup by its window ID, or "desktop" for whatever has the focus. |

## computer_windows

List the windows on a desktop box's screen, with the window IDs the other computer tools take. A device box has one, window 1, the device's screen.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | string | yes | The box's name or ID, from box_acquire or box_list. |
